# Synapse 2.0.19

Synapse AI builds a tool for an API that takes no key, such as Open-Meteo's weather forecast, instead of setting it aside; the line that moves a workflow from OpenAI Agent Builder says you can attach a screenshot; and a pip upgrade that installed and started no longer ends in an error.

## Fixed

- **An API that takes no key is built.** Asked for something a free, keyless API answers, Synapse AI could set that API aside with "this API takes its key in the URL, which I can't keep safely" and offer to build without it. Open-Meteo's weather forecast was one. It now builds the tool for an API that names no key. It also keeps a fixed value with a slash in the API's address, such as a time zone (`timezone=Europe/Lisbon`). An API that does take a key in its address is still set aside, now whichever way its key's name is written (`apiKey`, `client_secret`, `appid`).
- **The Agent Builder line says a screenshot works.** The "Move a workflow from OpenAI Agent Builder" line asks you to paste the workflow's Agents SDK code, attach a screenshot of it, or describe it in your own words. A screenshot has been read since 2.0.18.
- **A pip upgrade that installed and started says so.** After it installs the new version, updates the database and starts Synapse, an upgrade made with pip asks where Synapse is running. When that answer was empty or unreadable, the upgrade ended in a Python error, or in "Upgrade failed", although nothing had failed. It now ends by saying the new version is installed and was started, such as "Synapse 2.0.20 is installed and was started, but it didn't say where it is running. Check it with: synapse status".

An upgrade runs the version you already have, so pip upgrades get the last fix from the next release on.

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.19`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.0.x:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.
